credibility: Credibility Assessment: Marcus Doyle Marcus Doyle ("Doyle"), Team Supervisor, Member Services, Contact Center, was interviewed on September 18, 2026. He stated that he has had the team since February. 1 2 Doyle is the subject of the complaint. This section sets out his account on each disputed topic and compares it with the documents and the other witnesses, considering corroboration, consistency, plausibility and his interest in the outcome. The September 9 Huddle Remarks Asked whether he said "We'll see about Fridays" at the huddle, Doyle answered "Probably," explained that he meant they would see how the rotation worked out, and stated that the remark was not aimed at Leah Goldberg ("Goldberg"). 3 4 Goldberg and Jordan Kim ("Kim"), Member Services Representative, both reported Doyle using those words. 5 6 Doyle's account therefore matches theirs on the words spoken and differs on their meaning and target. On the "holy day" remark, Doyle said, "I might have said something like that," and described it as being about staffing in general rather than about Goldberg. 7 8 Kim stated that he heard Doyle say, "If everyone wanted their holy day off, nobody would work Fridays," from about six feet away. 9 Goldberg did not hear the remark herself and learned of it from Kim. 10 Doyle's answer is qualified rather than a denial, and the account he gave of its purpose differs from Goldberg's reading of events. Doyle denied saying that Goldberg should find a job that fits her religion, stating, "No. I never said that." 11 Kim did not hear such a remark and said he heard it only from Carla Rivera ("Rivera"). 12 Rivera, Workforce Management Analyst, Contact Center, told the investigator that she did not hear Doyle say anything about Goldberg's religion and never heard him say Goldberg should find another job. She said she told Kim only that Doyle had been "grumbling about the Friday requests." 13 14 Rivera's account is taken from the investigator's notes rather than a transcript. 15 No first-hand witness to the "find a job" remark is identified. The Handling of the Accommodation Request Doyle stated that Jordan Pierce, Regional Operations Manager, set the Q4 rotation at the regional level, that he did not think he had the authority to change it, and that he told Goldberg no on September 14. 16 17 His September 14 email said, "The rotation is set and I can't make exceptions for one person." 18 Doyle's explanation that he could not change the rotation is consistent with the wording of his denial. The Religious Accommodation Policy requires a supervisor who believes a request cannot be granted to consult HR before denying it. 24 Doyle did not describe whether he consulted HR before the denial. The Escalations Queue Removal Doyle stated that Rivera sent him a list of representatives without the new certification, that the requirement started on September 15, that he removed everyone on the list, that four people were on it, and that he did not pick anyone. 25 Rivera told the investigator that the certification became mandatory on September 15, that she emailed the September 10 list to all supervisors, and that Goldberg, Ngozi Okafor, Kevin Tran and Amy Bell were the four representatives on Doyle's team on it. 26 27 The change log records Doyle removing all four on September 16 between 7:05 and 7:07 AM, each with the reason "Cert not on file (LMS pull 9/10)." 28 Doyle's account matches Rivera's account and the log on the number of people removed, the source of the list and the timing. Doyle stated that he first learned of Goldberg's complaint when Priya Anand ("Anand"), HR Business Partner, called him on September 17 and that he did not know before. 32 Rivera stated that she did not know Goldberg had raised any complaint. 33 No other source in the case addresses when Doyle learned of the complaint. Doyle's General Position Doyle concluded his interview by stating, "I'm not against anyone's religion. I thought my hands were tied." 34 The investigator has recorded findings of not found on Allegation 1, found on Allegation 2, partly found on Allegation 3 and not found on Allegation 4.
client: The complaint. On September 15, 2026, Leah Goldberg, a Member Services Representative II in the Contact Center, filed a complaint about her supervisor, Marcus Doyle, Team Supervisor, Member Services. She alleged that he denied her request to avoid Friday evening shifts for Shabbat observance, did not consider a coworker's offered shift swap, and made comments suggesting disrespect for her religious practice. 1 Scope. The investigation covers three allegations under two policies. Two fall under the Religious Accommodation Policy: whether Doyle responded within five business days, and whether he considered and discussed alternatives and consulted HR before denying the request. One falls under the Anti-Harassment Policy: whether Doyle made remarks about religion or Goldberg's observance. Work done. Intake is complete. No interviews have taken place, and no findings have been made. Status. The initial investigation plan is awaiting review. Interviews and document collection are expected to follow once the plan is approved. The next update will be provided on [date of next update].
deadline: Yes. Doyle's reply was within the window, on its last day. Goldberg's request went to Doyle on Friday, September 4, and the policy requires a written response within five business days, excluding weekends and company holidays, with Labor Day on Monday, September 7 named as a holiday. 1 2 3 His denial email is dated Monday, September 14, at 5:48 PM. 4 Counting from September 4 and skipping the weekends and September 7, September 8 through 11 are business days 1 to 4 and September 14 is business day 5, so the reply was within five business days. That count does not include the start day and treats any time on the last day as within the window, and the policy text may be read differently on either point. The "ten days" in Goldberg's complaint is a calendar count, which includes the weekends and the holiday. 5 This only addresses timing. The policy's separate requirements to consider and discuss alternatives and to consult HR before denying are not part of this count. 6

finding3: ALLEGATION 3: Did Marcus Doyle make remarks about religion, or about Goldberg's religious observance, in connection with the Q4 Friday rotation, including at or after the team huddle (which the complainant gives as September 9, 2026), covering the "We'll see about Fridays" remark, the remark about employees wanting a "holy day" off, and the reported remark that Goldberg should find a job that fits her religion? FINDING: SUBSTANTIATED. First, the "We'll see about Fridays" remark at the September 9 huddle is established by three accounts that agree on its words. Leah Goldberg ("Goldberg"), Member Services Representative II, stated that when the rotation was discussed, Marcus Doyle ("Doyle"), Team Supervisor, Member Services, said "Fine." and then, looking directly at her, said "We'll see about Fridays." 1 Jordan Kim ("Kim"), Member Services Representative, who attended the huddle, recalled Doyle saying something like "Fine" and then "we'll see about Fridays." 2 Doyle, asked whether he said it, answered "Probably." 3 Doyle explained that he meant they would see how the rotation worked out and that the remark "wasn't aimed at Leah." 4 Kim stated that he did not think much of it at the time. 2 The remark was made, and it was made in the setting of Goldberg's pending request to be kept off Friday evenings, which she had emailed to Doyle five days earlier because she observes Shabbat. 5 Second, the "holy day" remark is supported by a first-hand witness. Kim stated that after the huddle Doyle, at his desk and "kind of loud," said, "If everyone wanted their holy day off, nobody would work Fridays," and that Kim heard it himself from about six feet away. 6 Goldberg did not hear the remark herself and learned of it from Kim afterwards. 7 Her complaint email likewise reported it as something Kim told her. 8 Doyle did not deny it. When asked whether he said those words, he responded, "I might have said something like that," and added that it "was about staffing in general, not about Leah." 9 Kim's first-hand account is therefore matched by Doyle's own partial admission, and the two differ only on what the remark was meant to convey. Third, Doyle's explanation that both remarks concerned staffing and the rotation does not displace the content of the words. The "holy day" remark refers to a religious observance by its own terms, and it was made on Friday scheduling while Goldberg's religious accommodation request was outstanding. 6 5 Doyle's account that he was not referring to Goldberg does not change that he made a remark about religion in connection with the Q4 Friday rotation. On the totality of the evidence, Doyle made the "We'll see about Fridays" remark at the September 9 huddle and the "holy day" remark afterwards, and both were remarks about religious observance in connection with the Friday rotation. Thus, based on a preponderance of the evidence, it is likely that Doyle made remarks about religion in connection with the Q4 Friday rotation, namely the "We'll see about Fridays" remark and the "holy day" remark. Note: I left the reported remark that Goldberg should find a job that fits her religion out of the finding, because the evidence does not support it. Kim said he heard it only from Carla Rivera and not himself, Doyle denied it, and Rivera said she never heard Doyle say it. 10 11 12 Also, the recorded finding for this allegation is "Partly found" and the Anti-Harassment Policy is recorded as Not Substantiated, so you may want to reconcile that with a "SUBSTANTIATED" label.
retaliation: Your conclusion holds up on this record: Allegation 4 looks not supported. You haven't spelled out your reasoning, so I'm testing the conclusion against the evidence. Uniform action: Doyle removed four reps in about two minutes, Goldberg, Okafor, Tran and Bell, each with the reason "Cert not on file (LMS pull 9/10)". 1 Goldberg believed she was the only one removed, but she qualified that with "as far as I know". 2 Okafor and Bell were never certified, so their removals were correct. 3 Source of the error: Rivera sent all supervisors the uncertified list on September 10, and the requirement became mandatory September 15. 4 Goldberg finished the course August 28, but the LMS didn't show it until September 11, after the pull. 5 Rivera attributes the error to the weekly vendor sync lag, and she restored Goldberg and Tran herself on September 21. 6 Knowledge: Doyle says he first learned of the complaint on September 17, the day after the removal. 7 Rivera says she didn't know about the complaint. 8 Two points cut the other way: Timing: The removal was the morning after the complaint. 9 10 Doyle's lack of knowledge rests on his own word. Nothing in the record independently shows when he found out. - The accommodation request as protected activity: Doyle indisputably knew of the September 4 request, and the policy treats requesting a religious accommodation as protected activity. 11 So the "no knowledge of the complaint" point doesn't cover that theory. What answers it is that the removal hit everyone on the list, not just her. The one gap that could change this is Doyle's handling. The Anti-Retaliation Policy expects managers acting against someone who recently engaged in protected activity to consult HR and document their reasons. 12 The log gives a reason, but the record shows no HR consultation and no check that Goldberg's status was current. That would be a process lapse, not evidence of motive. It would help to confirm that no one, such as Pierce or another supervisor, told Doyle about the complaint before September 17.
harassment: The strongest argument is that this is a single, undirected remark about staffing, and it falls short of the policy's threshold. The policy requires more than a remark about religion. Harassment is defined as unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic that is "sufficiently severe or pervasive to create an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment, or that affects the terms and conditions of employment." 1 One sentence, once, is hard to call pervasive. - It isn't the kind of conduct the policy lists. The verbal examples are things like "Offensive jokes, slurs, epithets, or name-calling" and "Threats, intimidation, or hostile language." 2 Kim describes Doyle as "talking to himself, kind of loud" at his desk, which is not a joke, slur, threat or insult aimed at anyone. 3 It wasn't directed at Goldberg. She did not hear it herself and learned of it from Kim. 4 Doyle says he "might have said something like that" and that it was about staffing in general. 5 Read that way, it is a complaint about Friday coverage that happens to use a religious word. - Nothing around it supplies the missing severity. The one remark that would show hostility toward her religion, that she should find a job that fits it, rests only on Kim relaying what Rivera allegedly told him. Kim didn't hear it, Doyle denies it, and Rivera says she never heard Doyle say it or anything about Goldberg's religion. 6 7 8 The real grievance sits under another policy. Goldberg's complaint is that her request was ignored and denied. 9 That is Allegation 1 and 2 territory under the Religious Accommodation Policy, which is where any effect on her terms of employment would be addressed, so the remark need not carry it. This is one side of the argument. The reply is that the remark was made by her supervisor while her request was pending, and that is the context in which a tribunal would read it.
gaps: The biggest gaps are on allegations 2 and 4. Allegation 1 turns on a rule you can apply to the dates you already have, and allegation 3 is mostly settled except for the "find a job" remark. Allegation 1 (timing): The record shows no earlier written response from Doyle. Goldberg emailed on September 4, and Doyle's only reply in Exhibit A is dated September 14. 1 2 The policy gives five business days, excluding weekends and company holidays, and lists Labor Day, September 7, as a holiday. 3 4 Doyle was never asked about timing. He only said he told her no on the 14th. 5 Ask him whether he responded in any form before the 14th, and check that nothing else went to Goldberg in writing. Allegation 2 (alternatives and HR): HR consultation: The policy requires it before a denial. 6 Doyle wasn't asked whether he consulted HR, and no communication between him and HR is in the record. - Pierce: Pierce's August 24 email says supervisors may approve swaps between reps with the same skills. 7 Doyle says he didn't think swaps were allowed during the Q4 rollout. 8 Pierce isn't among the people on the case. Without his account, or any later guidance, there is nothing to test Doyle's belief or show where it came from. - Date mismatch: Goldberg dates the rotation announcement August 31, but the Pierce email is dated August 24. 9 10 Look for a separate August 31 communication. Allegation 3 (remarks): "Find a job" remark: It rests on Rivera, through Kim. Kim says he heard it only from her. 11 Rivera's account is Anand's notes rather than a transcript, and she denies saying it. 12 13 No date is given for the remark. Nobody else has been asked. - Other huddle attendees: None have been interviewed. They could speak to the huddle remark and the desk remark. Allegation 4 (retaliation): When Doyle learned of the complaint: This is the central gap. He says he first learned on September 17. 14 The record has nothing independent on this, such as who else knew by September 16 or whether HR or anyone else contacted him earlier. - Rivera's September 10 email: Rivera says she emailed the list to all supervisors. 15 Only her notes are in the record, not the email or the vendor sync records. The log's "LMS pull 9/10" entry ties to the list. 16 - Goldberg's completion email: She says she has it, 17 but it isn't in the record. - HR consultation and documentation: Nothing shows Doyle consulted HR or documented his reasons before removing someone who had recently requested an accommodation. The Anti-Retaliation Policy expects both. 18 19

executive: Leah Goldberg ("Goldberg"), a Member Services Representative II in the Contact Center at Harlow & Pine Credit Union (the "Company"), submitted a formal complaint to HR Business Partner Priya Anand on September 15, 2026. The complaint concerned her supervisor, Marcus Doyle ("Doyle"), Team Supervisor, Member Services. Goldberg alleged that Doyle mishandled her request to be kept off Friday evening shifts for Shabbat observance and made comments showing disrespect for her religious practice. The complaint and intake record also raised her removal from the escalations queue, which carries a pay differential, on September 16, 2026. 1 2 Four allegations were investigated under three policies: whether Doyle failed to respond within five business days (Religious Accommodation Policy); whether he denied the request without considering and discussing alternatives, including a coworker's shift swap, and without consulting HR (Religious Accommodation Policy); whether he made remarks about religion or Goldberg's observance (Anti-Harassment Policy); and whether he removed Goldberg from the escalations queue because of her accommodation request or HR complaint (Anti-Retaliation Policy). The investigator's findings are as follows. The Religious Accommodation Policy was substantiated. The allegation that Doyle failed to respond within five business days was not found, and the allegation that he denied the request without considering and discussing alternatives was found. The Anti-Harassment Policy was not substantiated, with the allegation about religious remarks partly found. The Anti-Retaliation Policy was not substantiated, as the allegation that Doyle removed Goldberg from the escalations queue because of her request or complaint was not found.
redraft: ALLEGATION 3: Did Marcus Doyle make remarks about religion, or about Goldberg's religious observance, in connection with the Q4 Friday rotation, including at or after the team huddle (which the complainant gives as September 9, 2026)? This covers the "We'll see about Fridays" remark, the remark about employees wanting a "holy day" off, and the reported remark that Goldberg should find a job that fits her religion. FINDING: NOT SUBSTANTIATED. First, the Anti-Harassment Policy defines harassment as "unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic that is sufficiently severe or pervasive to create an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment, or that affects the terms and conditions of employment." 1 Religion is a protected characteristic under the policy. 2 The question is therefore whether the remarks that were made, taken together, reached that threshold. Second, the "We'll see about Fridays" remark was made. Goldberg stated that when the rotation was discussed at the September 9 huddle Doyle said "Fine." and then, looking at her, said "We'll see about Fridays." 3 Kim, who attended the huddle, recalled Doyle saying "Fine" and then "we'll see about Fridays," and said he did not think much of it at the time. 4 Doyle said he "[p]robably" said it, that he meant they would see how the rotation worked out, and that it was not aimed at Goldberg. 5 The words themselves make no reference to religion, and Kim's contemporaneous reaction was that they were unremarkable. Third, the "holy day" remark was made. Kim stated that after the huddle Doyle, at his desk and "kind of loud," said, "If everyone wanted their holy day off, nobody would work Fridays," and that Kim heard this himself from about six feet away. 6 Doyle said he "might have said something like that" and that it was about staffing in general, not about Goldberg. 7 Goldberg did not hear the remark herself and learned of it from Kim. 8 The remark referred to a religious concept, and it was made by Goldberg's supervisor in the context of her pending request. It was, however, a single comment, made in the course of discussing staffing and not addressed to Goldberg, and the record describes no insult, epithet, joke or threat directed at her or at her religion. Fourth, the evidence does not establish that Doyle said Goldberg should find a job that fits her religion. Kim stated that Carla Rivera told him Doyle said this, that he did not hear it himself, and that he knew of it only from Rivera. 9 Rivera, Workforce Management Analyst, Contact Center, said she did not hear Doyle say anything about Goldberg's religion, that she told Kim only that Doyle had been "grumbling about the Friday requests," and that she never heard Doyle say Goldberg should find another job. 10 Doyle denied saying it. 11 No first-hand witness supports the remark. Fifth, the record does not show a pattern of conduct. Goldberg identified the huddle remark and the second-hand "holy day" remark as the comments at issue and added that she does not feel her religion is respected on the team. 12 Nothing in the record describes further religious remarks over time, and Goldberg did not describe any in her interview. 13 Two remarks on one day, one of them facially neutral, are not pervasive. Sixth, the remarks did not alter the terms and conditions of Goldberg's employment.
